context_candidates.text: These patterns connect the report’s monitoring to the concerns of middle-income economies. More work and better-paying work help people escape poverty (refer to chapter 4). Stable, well-paid jobs also protect against falling back into poverty, and they therefore help households climb from vulnerability to security, an agenda that has particular force in locations where the vulnerable group is largest. Vulnerability to climate-related hazards—a distinct concept, reflecting the lack of the means to cope if a hazard strikes rather than the risk of falling back into poverty—extends well above the poverty line (refer to chapter 3). Vulnerability in this case means that middle-class households are also exposed to risk if social protection and financial services are lacking. The $8.30 line and the $28.00 prosperity standard are precisely the boundaries within which the middle class is found.

Measured against these thresholds, the global middle class has grown substantially since 2000, roughly doubling as a share of the world’s population.

The group living on between $3.00 and $8.30 a day, however, has remained close to a third of the world’s population throughout the period. Among large numbers of people, the exit from extreme poverty has thus represented an exit into vulnerability rather than into security.

Applying the vulnerability approach to the World Bank’s harmonized household surveys—estimating, for each economy, the probability that a household is living on less than the poverty line of the relevant income group over a few years, and identifying the consumption level at which this probability becomes low—yields economic security lines of about $6.00, $7.00, and $14.00 a day for the three income groups. This is roughly twice the corresponding poverty lines, but with wide variation across economies (Bolch et al. 2026). The threshold also shifts with the risks households face. In Europe and Central Asia, the income needed to maintain a low probability of falling into poverty rose by about 10 percent in real terms between 2008 and 2018 as the shocks pushing households into poverty grew larger (Bussolo et al. 2025). There is no fixed income at which security begins. The boundary of the

[3fac16b8c36e67393af2577c13d1120cc3b0eafe580768da97b3a4b63640439e | https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/entities/publication/6fbbb475-58f1-49e0-90b3-f329e8124694 | page 54]
22 POVERTY , PROSPERITY , AND PLANET REPORT 2026 in 2000 to a majority by 2026, and extreme poverty has all but disappeared. In today’s lower-middle-income economies, the group living on between $3.00 and $8.30 a day is now the largest, and the middle class, though growing, remains a minority. In low-income economies, the distribution has barely shifted. About half the population is still living on less than $3.00 a day, and the middle class is negligible. High-income economies, by contrast, are composed almost entirely of households living on more than $8.30 a day, and the majority are above the prosperity standard.
